Nik Nocturnal, known for his presence on YouTube as a musician, brings a distinct guitar style that is both intricate and heavy. Andy Cizek, who also serves as the vocalist for the pop-punk band WVNDER and an ambient rock project, lends his dynamic vocal abilities to the track, ranging from melodic singing to aggressive screams.

The song itself is a journey through dark and emotive themes, with the instrumentation creating a dense and immersive soundscape. The guitar work is a standout feature, offering a mix of punishing riffs and atmospheric melodies that complement the vocal delivery. The rhythm section, though not highlighted by permanent band members, supports the song with precision and adds to the overall intensity.

Lyrically, “Bathed in Solitude” delves into themes of inner turmoil, isolation, and a confrontation with darker aspects of the self. The lyrics are introspective and resonate with a sense of raw honesty and vulnerability. The song’s structure takes the listener through various phases of intensity, with quieter, introspective moments building into powerful, cathartic crescendos.

The production quality of the track is noteworthy, balancing clarity with a sense of raw energy. Each element, from the vocals to the instruments, is given space to shine, creating a cohesive and impactful listening experience.

Overall, “Bathed in Solitude” is a testament to Termina’s ability to craft music that is both emotionally resonant and technically impressive. It’s a track that should appeal to fans of modern metal and anyone who appreciates music that combines technical skill with deep emotional expression.

For a review of the song music, structure, video, and related things, watch the reaction video posted above.

The Song, Meaning & Lyrics

“Illumishade’s song ‘Enemy’ is a riveting and intense musical journey, encapsulating a blend of emotions and themes that resonate deeply with the complexities of human relationships and societal dynamics. The song opens with a palpable sense of ‘Tension,’ immediately setting the stage for a narrative that delves into the struggles of trust, betrayal, and the internal battles we face.

The lyrics ‘Leave your ways and count your days / The earth has been shaken’ suggest a world in turmoil, perhaps reflecting on personal upheaval or broader societal unrest. This theme of disruption continues with ‘Dissension / Positions are taken,’ painting a picture of conflict and division, where individuals are forced to take sides, metaphorically ‘grinding their axes’ and ‘raising their flags.’

A poignant moment in the song is the line ‘I watch the figures in the clouds / To love you is to see me dying.’ This lyric beautifully captures the pain and vulnerability of loving someone in a tumultuous relationship or environment. It speaks to the heartache of feeling disconnected and misunderstood, a theme that is further explored in the chorus.

The chorus, ‘How can I trust someone I do not understand / And how can I reach for the tips of a burning hand,’ is particularly striking. It encapsulates the core dilemma of the song – the challenge of building trust in a relationship fraught with suspicion and misunderstanding. The imagery of reaching for a ‘burning hand’ powerfully conveys the risk and fear involved in trying to connect with someone who might cause pain.

As the song progresses, it touches on themes of deception (‘They will lie and they will grin’) and the need for vigilance against corruption (‘Corruption must not win’). This reflects a broader commentary on societal issues, where appearances can be deceiving, and the truth is often obscured by lies and manipulation.

The latter part of the song introduces a more introspective element with ‘I’ve never felt so alone in my skin / I didn’t know I had this monster hiding.’ This reveals a personal struggle, an internal battle with one’s own demons and insecurities. It’s a powerful admission of the often-hidden turmoil that many people face.

The song concludes with a sense of unity and shared destiny (‘Here we stand beneath the ether / Bound to our sole desire’), yet there’s an underlying tension, as this unity involves ‘sinking our teeth into each other.’ The final lines, ‘Our ashes remember the arguments / The monster will scour the earth for innocence,’ leave the listener with a haunting reminder of the lasting impact of conflict and the ongoing search for purity and understanding in a complex world.

Overall, ‘Enemy’ by Illumishade is a masterful blend of poetic lyricism and emotive storytelling, capturing the essence of human conflict, the struggle for understanding, and the search for connection in a divided world.”

Cypecore, known for their distinctive blend of melodic death metal and futuristic themes, delivers an immersive auditory experience with their track “Patient Zero.” This song, like much of their work, is not just a musical composition but a narrative journey set against a backdrop of a dystopian universe. The band’s choice to don dystopian garb is a deliberate and integral part of their identity, serving as a visual extension of their music’s thematic focus on a post-apocalyptic world.

“Patient Zero” is a powerful representation of Cypecore’s unique style. The song combines relentless guitar riffs, pounding drums, and commanding vocals to create a sound that is both aggressive and melodically captivating. The track opens with an eerie, atmospheric intro that sets the tone for a story of desolation and survival. As the song progresses, the intensity builds, mirroring the narrative of a world ravaged by disease and conflict – themes that are central to the band’s overarching concept.

The band’s decision to dress in dystopian attire is more than just an aesthetic choice; it’s a narrative tool that enhances the storytelling aspect of their music. Lyrically, “Patient Zero” delves into the despair and resilience of humanity in the face of a global catastrophe. The song’s protagonist, presumably the titular “Patient Zero,” symbolizes both the origin of the calamity and the potential for redemption. This duality is reflected in the vocal delivery, which oscillates between guttural growls and hauntingly clear melodies, embodying the conflict between hope and despair.

In conclusion, Cypecore’s “Patient Zero” is a testament to the band’s ability to weave complex narratives through their music. Their choice to dress in dystopian garb is a critical component of their storytelling, adding a visual dimension that complements their thematic exploration of a ravaged world. title.rendered: Enthralling Reaction to Enterprise Earth’s song “Casket of Rust”

content.rendered:
Enterprise Earth’s latest offering, ‘Casket of Rust,’ is a masterful symphony of chaos, a veritable odyssey through the realms of heavy metal. From the very first note, the song ensnares the listener in a labyrinthine embrace of sound, each twist and turn more captivating than the last.

The track opens with a barrage of guitars, their riffs a tumultuous sea upon which the drums crash like thunderous waves. This is not mere noise, but a carefully orchestrated tempest, each element contributing to an overwhelming sense of awe. The guitar work is nothing short of prodigious, weaving intricate patterns that dazzle with their complexity and sheer speed.

At the helm of this sonic juggernaut is the vocal performance, a tour de force of guttural roars and piercing screams. It’s a voice that seems to channel the very essence of the genre, embodying both its raw power and its nuanced depths. The lyrics themselves are a tapestry of dark imagery and profound introspection, inviting the listener to delve into a world of existential dread and morbid fascination.

But what truly sets ‘Casket of Rust’ apart is its ability to marry this maelstrom of sound with moments of surprising delicacy. Amidst the fury, there are interludes of haunting melody, brief respites that serve to highlight the intensity of the surrounding storm. These passages are not mere afterthoughts but integral parts of the song’s narrative, guiding the listener through its many layers.

In ‘Casket of Rust,’ Enterprise Earth has not just created a song but an experience. It’s a piece that demands attention, not just for its technical prowess but for the emotional journey it offers. This is a band at the height of its powers, unafraid to push boundaries and explore the darker corners of the human psyche. For fans of the genre, it’s an essential listen, a reminder of why we turn to music to feel something profound and unsettling. In a word, ‘Casket of Rust’ is a masterpiece, a dazzling display of esoteric talent and epic cacophony that will resonate long after the final note has faded.

title.rendered: Reaction to Sum 41’s Hilarious New Song “Rise Up”

Known for their punk rock roots, Sum 41 takes a refreshing detour with this song, infusing it with playful lyrics and upbeat rhythms that are both catchy and amusing. The band’s ability to weave humor into their music without losing their edge is impressive. ‘Rise Up’ is not just a song; it’s a playful jab that reminds us not to take everything so seriously. The chorus is particularly infectious, likely to get stuck in your head for hours. It’s a reminder of Sum 41’s talent for creating music that’s not only energetic and entertaining but also resonates with their audience on a different level.

title.rendered: Reaction to Zee Mustang of Lesbian Bed Death’s Song “Roadkill”

content.rendered:
Lesbian Bed Death’s latest track ‘Roadkill’ hits the scene with all the subtlety of a neon-painted hearse in a funeral procession. If you’re into a brand of rock that sounds like it was brewed in a cauldron of gothic clichés and sprinkled with a dash of punk rebellion, then this might just be your jam.

The song trudges along with guitar riffs that are as predictable as a horror movie plot, and lyrics that seem to have been dug up from the graveyard of teenage angst. The band does show some skill, clinging to their rock roots like a lifeline, but the overall effect is akin to wearing sunglasses at night – trying a bit too hard to be cool. It’s clear they’re having a blast, and there’s a certain charm to their commitment to the goth-punk aesthetic, but let’s just say it’s an acquired taste. ‘Roadkill’ is okay rock ‘n’ roll – it’s got the right ingredients, but it’s like ordering a cocktail only to realize you prefer beer. Not exactly my cup of tea, but hey, to each their own brand of musical necromancy.

title.rendered: Reaction to Hand of Juno’s Esoteric “We’ve Built the Line” Song in Leather THAT BASS!

content.rendered:
Hand of Juno’s latest offering, ‘We’ve Built the Line,’ is a smorgasbord of esoteric charm and industrial grit, wrapped in an aesthetic that’s as intriguing as the music itself. The video is a visual feast, dominated by leather and avant-garde outfits that seem to scream rebellion with every stitch. The band members are decked out in an array of leather ensembles that range from dystopian chic to edgy punk, each outfit seemingly tailored to enhance their individual musical personas.

A standout moment in the video is the bass player, whose name I unfortunately don’t have, commanding attention not just with her attire but with her instrument’s deep, smacklicious thump. She’s draped in a sleek leather outfit that perfectly encapsulates the blend of power and allure, embodying the spirit of the song. Her presence is magnetic, and when she sexily drops those bass lines, it’s more than just a musical moment; it’s a statement.

The bass itself is a character in its own right, with a sound so rich and textured it feels like an auditory pulse driving the song forward. It adds a weighty, sensual undercurrent to the tune, perfectly complementing the industrial overtones and the visually striking leather aesthetics of the video.

‘We’ve Built the Line’ is not just a song; it’s an experience. Hand of Juno has managed to create a piece that’s as much about visual storytelling as it is about auditory excellence. The leather-laden visuals and the thumping bass lines come together to create a piece that’s edgy, esoteric, and utterly captivating.

title.rendered: Flummoxed Reaction to I Am Your God’s, Not Me, Them, Their Song “Another Day to Die”

content.rendered:
A harsh verdict awaits.

I Am Your God’s latest track, “Another Day to Die,” seems to be an ode to the overused metal tropes that many of us hoped had been laid to rest. Right from the get-go, the song plunges into a whirlpool of angst and rebellion, a concoction we’ve tasted far too many times.

The opening riff is as predictable as a sunrise, lacking the innovative edge that could have set it apart in a sea of metal mediocrity. It’s like they stumbled upon a ‘Metal Riffs for Dummies’ book and decided that was all the inspiration they needed. And let’s talk about the lyrics – a patchwork of every metal cliché you can think of, stitched together with the subtlety of a sledgehammer. Lines like “Walking through the shadows, the reaper’s my only friend” feel like a half-hearted nod to the genre’s greats, minus the depth and ingenuity.

The vocal performance, while technically proficient, comes off as a caricature of metal angst. It’s as if the lead singer is trying to channel every metal frontman ever, ending up as a jack-of-all-trades, master of none. The drumming and bass, while tight, don’t venture beyond the safe confines of metal conventions. They’re like the dependable sidekicks in a superhero movie – there, but hardly memorable.

But hey, it’s not all doom and gloom. The guitar solo midway is a brief glimmer of hope, showcasing some genuine skill. It’s like finding a diamond in a rough – a rough that’s unfortunately all too familiar and worn out.

In the grand scheme of metal, “Another Day to Die” is unlikely to be the track that propels I Am Your God to the pantheon of metal legends. It’s more like a comfort blanket for those who like their metal unchallenging and wrapped in familiarity. For the rest of us, it’s just another day, another predictable metal track.

title.rendered: The Bellted Out Tones of Rolling Quartz’s Song “Fearless”

content.rendered:
As I sat down to immerse myself in Rolling Quartz’s latest offering, “Fearless,” I felt a sense of anticipation tinged with a quirky excitement. In a world where music often feels like a rehearsed echo, this track promised something different. And oh, did it deliver.

Right from the get-go, “Fearless” serves up a blend of raw energy and polished musicianship that’s as refreshing as a cool breeze on a stifling summer day. The opening riffs are a siren call to anyone who appreciates the art of the guitar, a tip of the hat to the greats while carving out a unique identity. It’s like finding an unexplored path in a familiar forest – exhilarating, a bit mysterious, but inviting.

The vocals are an enchanting mix of power and vulnerability. There’s a distinct flavor here, one that doesn’t just ride the melody but dances around it, playing a game of hide and seek with the listener’s expectations. It’s quirky, yes, but in the best way possible. Like finding an oddly shaped cloud that perfectly reflects your mood.

Lyrically, “Fearless” is a tapestry of bold strokes and fine details as it dances between english and japanese. The message is empowering, a clarion call to embrace our fears and emerge stronger. But it’s delivered with a subtlety that invites introspection rather than demanding attention. It’s like a wise friend speaking in a calm, knowing tone – confident, but never overbearing.

The production quality strikes a fine balance between polished and authentic. Every instrument finds its place in the mix without overshadowing the others. The result is a sound that’s clean but not sterile, professional but not soulless. It’s the musical equivalent of a perfectly brewed cup of coffee – just the right amount of kick, without any bitterness.

title.rendered: Another Head Shattering Brand of Sacrifice song “Between Death and Dreams”

The drumming is nothing short of explosive, providing a solid backbone to the chaos with precise blasts and fills. The bass, though often overshadowed in this genre, makes its presence felt with a deep growl that complements the guitars and drums perfectly.

The vocals on “Between Death and Dreams” are a highlight, showcasing a range that moves from guttural growls to piercing screams. This vocal diversity adds a layer of emotional intensity to the track, conveying a sense of despair and longing that is palpable. The lyrics are poetic and thought-provoking, exploring themes of existential dread and the search for meaning in a seemingly indifferent universe.

Production-wise, the song is masterfully crafted. The mix balances clarity with raw power, allowing each element of the band’s sound to shine through without sacrificing the overall impact of the music. The use of atmospheric elements and subtle electronic textures adds depth to the track, creating moments of eerie calm amidst the storm.

content.rendered:
Enterprise Earth’s new song “Blood & Teeth” from their album “Death: An Anthology” has been met with varied reactions from critics and fans alike, reflecting a diverse palette of musical influences and showcasing the band’s dynamic range.

MetalSucks praises the album for its variety, highlighting the new vocalist Travis Worland’s dynamic performance across different vocal styles. Although they were not fans of the melodic parts in “Blood & Teeth,” they commend the album for its impressive riffs and solos that make up for any shortcomings.

Lambgoat provides insight into the thematic depth of “Blood & Teeth,” describing it as a gut-wrenching story of poisonous attachment. The song is noted for its elaborate composition, moving through different musical sections, from a clean piano intro to a heavy breakdown. The track is seen as the most expressive on the album, delivering an intense emotional experience.

Distorted Sound Magazine gives the album a high rating, appreciating the ambitious mix of deathcore with other metal influences. “Blood & Teeth” is mentioned as part of the album’s stunning highs, offering a mix of melodic death verses and soaring melodies that push the confines of deathcore.

Wall of Sound, however, offers a more critical view. While acknowledging the album’s ambition and the earworm quality of tracks like “King of Ruination,” the review suggests that “Blood & Teeth” presents jarring saccharine cleans and metalcore-inspired guitar runs that feel somewhat out of place. Despite this, the album is seen as a step in the right direction for the band.

This diverse feedback underscores Enterprise Earth’s evolution, with “Blood & Teeth” standing out as a testament to their expansive approach to deathcore, blending brutality with melodic and emotional depth. The song, and the album as a whole, seems to invite both old fans and new listeners to explore the band’s ambitious musical journey.

title.rendered: Becoming a little more human pondering human becoming with Calva Louise

content.rendered:
“Human Becoming” by Calva Louise is an exhilarating journey through sound, an audacious leap into the uncharted territories of musical composition that defies conventional boundaries and expectations. From the first note, it’s clear that this isn’t just another album; it’s a manifesto of innovation, a declaration of artistic freedom that resonates with the bold spirit of its creators.

What sets “Human Becoming” apart is how it eschews the standard verse-chorus mold, opting instead for a more fluid and dynamic structure that captivates and surprises at every turn. This isn’t music that you merely listen to; it’s an experience that engulfs you, demanding your full attention and rewarding it with layers of complexity and emotion that unfold with each listen.

The stylistic choices made throughout the album are nothing short of visionary. Tracks seamlessly blend elements of punk, electronic, and psychedelic rock, creating a soundscape that is both eclectic and cohesive. The use of synths and guitars is particularly noteworthy, weaving together melodies and riffs that are at once familiar and utterly unique. The vocals, too, are a highlight, ranging from ethereal whispers to powerful crescendos that convey a spectrum of human emotions and experiences.

Following the algorithm to “Human Becoming” feels like stumbling upon a hidden gem, a reminder of the magic that happens when artists dare to venture beyond the conventional and into the realm of the extraordinary. Calva Louise has not just created an album; they’ve crafted a masterpiece that challenges and expands the listener’s understanding of what music can be.

As a fan, the excitement of experiencing “Human Becoming” is akin to witnessing the unveiling of a masterpiece. It’s a thrilling reminder of the endless possibilities that lie in the pursuit of creative expression. This album is a beacon for those yearning for something different, something that doesn’t just conform to the mainstream but reshapes it in its own image.

title.rendered: Reacting to Calva Louise’s Back to “Square One”, and “The Feast is Over”

content.rendered:
After the last reaction video I had to queue up another Calva Louise tune. What I did not expect was what the next tune would be. I was kind of blown away when it melted into further genres, heavier rock, more guitar that I didn’t expect, and other vocal and stylistic changes that the previous song just didn’t set my expectations to. This new song was an entirely different creation with an entirely different vibe, feel, meaning, and aura – completely outside of theme from the previous.

I write all that with emphasis because no matter the band it is extremely rare when any artist or band deviates to this degree. Usually when an artist deviates it’s less than well accepted and often kind of – let’s be honest – a train wreck. Sometimes bands pull it off but pull it off is as rare as the deviations themselves. Calva Louise flawlessly moves between, and even merges these styles, deviations, and other variances beautifully!

The two songs in this VLOG, are from Calva Louise’s recent series of songs—”Third Class Citizen”, “Feast is Over”, “Square One”, and “Over The Threshold”—which showcases the band’s dynamic range and innovative spirit in the modern punk and alternative rock scene. Each track not only stands on its own with unique energy and storytelling but also contributes to a cohesive narrative when listened to as a series, reflecting on themes of struggle, resilience, and rebellion against societal constraints – specifically in the videos the world in which has been created that the songs are in reflection of. Spider invasion and all!

“Third Class Citizen” kicks off with an electrifying energy, combining gritty guitar riffs with anthemic choruses. The song is a powerful opener, setting a tone of defiance and dissatisfaction with the status quo. It’s an urgent call to awareness, wrapped in the band’s signature blend of punk ferocity and catchy melodies.

“Feast is Over” shifts gears slightly, presenting a more introspective yet equally compelling perspective. The track delves into the aftermath of excess and the realization that change is necessary. Musically, it balances between explosive moments and quieter, more reflective passages, showcasing the band’s ability to navigate complex emotional landscapes with finesse.

“Square One” represents a moment of introspection and the acknowledgment of needing to start anew. Its lyrics resonate with the feeling of being stuck but yearning for a breakthrough. The musical arrangement complements this sentiment perfectly, with a mix of driving rhythms and moments of melodic contemplation, creating a sense of hope amidst uncertainty.

Finally, “Over The Threshold” concludes the series on a note of triumph over adversity. It encapsulates the journey from feeling like a third-class citizen to overcoming barriers. The song is a rousing finale, bursting with optimism and the determination to move forward. It’s a celebration of resilience, with an infectious energy that encourages listeners to push through their own thresholds.

Together, these four tracks are a testament to Calva Louise’s artistry and their ability to convey complex emotions through a blend of sharp lyrics, compelling melodies, and high-energy performances. The series not only reinforces the band’s place in the punk and alternative rock landscape but also pushes the genre forward, proving that music can be both a mirror to our times and a hammer with which to shape them.

These two songs as stated, are two of a 4 part series of songs. The others, including these two, in order, are as follows:

Part 1 “Third Class Citizen“
Part 2 “Feast is Over“
Part 3 “Square One“
Part 4 “Over The Threshold“

Each track reflects themes of struggle, resilience, and rebellion against societal constraints, contributing to a cohesive narrative and pushing the genre forward with sharp lyrics and high-energy performances.

content.rendered:
Australian progressive metalcore band known for their boundary-pushing soundscapes and thought-provoking lyrics, takes listeners on a haunting journey with their track “Dante.” Released as part of their album “Singularity,” “Dante” stands out as a visceral exploration of existential themes and inner turmoil.

From the moment the song begins, Northlane’s trademark blend of atmospheric synths, crushing guitars, and intricate drumming sets a foreboding tone. The ethereal intro gradually builds suspense, drawing listeners into a sonic landscape that feels both vast and claustrophobic.

Marcus Bridge’s vocals soar and growl with equal intensity, conveying a sense of desperation and defiance. His delivery is emotionally charged, capturing the inner conflict depicted in the lyrics. Each word feels like a battle cry against the void, as if grappling with the existential dread that permeates the song.

Thematically, “Dante” delves into the depths of the human psyche, drawing parallels to the journey through Dante Alighieri’s “Inferno.” The lyrics paint vivid imagery of inner turmoil, existential crisis, and the quest for meaning in a seemingly indifferent universe. Lines like “I’m lost inside my head again / This darkness never ends” resonate with a raw honesty, tapping into universal struggles with self-doubt and introspection.

Instrumentally, “Dante” showcases Northlane’s technical prowess and knack for blending aggression with melody. The guitar riffs are razor-sharp yet melodic, serving as the perfect backdrop for Bridge’s emotive vocals. The rhythm section drives the song forward with relentless energy, adding layers of complexity to the overall composition.

As the song progresses, it reaches a climax of cathartic release, with Bridge’s vocals reaching a fever pitch amidst a cacophony of swirling guitars and thunderous drums. It’s a moment of raw vulnerability and raw power, encapsulating the emotional intensity that defines Northlane’s music.

“Dante” certainly captivates with its haunting atmosphere, emotive vocals, and intricate instrumentation, showcasing the band’s talent for creating deeply evocative music. However, despite its strengths, the track falls short of its full potential. While the thematic exploration of existentialism and inner turmoil is compelling, the song’s structure occasionally feels formulaic, lacking some of the experimental flair seen in other Northlane compositions. Additionally, while Marcus Bridge’s vocals are undeniably powerful, there are moments where they seem restrained, leaving listeners longing for more moments of raw intensity and vulnerability. With a slightly more adventurous approach to songwriting and a willingness to push the boundaries even further, “Dante” could have soared to even greater heights, solidifying its place as a standout in Northlane’s discography.

title.rendered: Architects’ “Seeing Red” Review: A Cathartic Manifesto Against Doubters

content.rendered:
Architects have never been a band to shy away from confronting criticism or evolving their sound. With their latest single, “Seeing Red,” they not only confront but also pulverize any doubts about their intensity and commitment to their craft. The song not only serves as a blistering anthem but also as a sly retort to those who claim they’ve softened over the years.

From the opening riff, “Seeing Red” unleashes a tsunami of aggression, with pounding drums and searing guitars that set the stage for vocalist Sam Carter’s ferocious delivery. Lyrically, the track is a declaration of resilience, with Carter confronting the naysayers head-on. The line “You thought I’d mellowed out, I’m here to prove you wrong” serves as a rallying cry for both the band and their fans.

What truly sets “Seeing Red” apart, however, is its clever incorporation of the “blegh” moment—a signature element of Architects’ sound. In this song, the “blegh” not only punctuates the raw emotion of the music but also serves as a tongue-in-cheek acknowledgment of the band’s self-awareness. By embracing this moment with gusto, Architects not only reclaim their hardcore roots but also offer a wink to those who doubted them.

In the context of the song’s theme, the “blegh” becomes a symbol of defiance—a sonic middle finger to anyone who dared to question the band’s authenticity. It’s a moment that is both hilarious and utterly timely, reminding listeners that Architects are not only capable of delivering punishing breakdowns but also of poking fun at themselves in the process.

“Seeing Red” is more than just a song; it’s a manifesto—no, a punch to the face-an assertion of identity and a declaration of intent. With its blistering energy and razor-sharp lyrics, it reaffirms Architects’ status as one of the most vital bands in modern metalcore. So to those who thought they’d gotten soft, “Seeing Red” is the perfect response: a sonic punch in the face that leaves no doubt about where Architects stand.

Christoph Schultz’s powerful vocals provide a compelling narrative to the song, exploring themes of sacrifice, resilience, and self-discovery. His emotive delivery adds depth and intensity to the lyrics, resonating with listeners on a visceral level.

The collaboration between Unprocessed and Polyphia demonstrates the mutual respect and admiration between these two innovative bands. By joining forces, they have created a song that pushes the boundaries of progressive metal, showcasing the incredible talent and creativity of all involved. “Die on The Cross of the Martyr” stands as a testament to the collaborative spirit of the metal community and further solidifies Unprocessed and Polyphia’s positions as leading forces in the genre.

title.rendered: WTF is this, BMTH and Babymetal performing Kingslayer! Smoke up first!

content.rendered:
Alright, let’s get into the depths of musical alchemy with “Kingslayer,” a monumental collaboration between Bring Me The Horizon (BMTH) and BABYMETAL that’s been rattling the senses of the metal community. Crank up the volume, ignite the senses (with whatever helps you vibe), and prepare for a journey through an audacious blend of metalcore ferocity and kawaii metal charm.

From the get-go, “Kingslayer” detonates into your eardrums with a barrage of electronic elements, setting a frenetic pace that’s both exhilarating and somewhat disorienting – in the best way possible. BMTH has always been at the forefront of pushing boundaries within the metalcore genre, but with BABYMETAL’s inclusion, they’ve dialed the unpredictability factor up to eleven.

The track is a masterful chaos of genres, melding the growling intensity of Oli Sykes’ vocals with the pristine, high-energy delivery of SU-METAL and MOAMETAL. The contrast is nothing short of electrifying, creating a sonic duality that’s as compelling as it is unique. The lyrical content, diving into themes of rebellion against corruption and tyranny, is delivered with such conviction that it’s impossible not to be swept up in the rallying cry.

Instrumentally, “Kingslayer” is a maelstrom of crushing riffs, thunderous drums, and synth-driven landscapes that feel like a cybernetic battlefield. BMTH’s prowess in crafting infectious melodies shines through, even as they intertwine with BABYMETAL’s signature blend of J-pop and metal, resulting in a soundscape that’s both aggressive and absurdly catchy.

The production on this track deserves a nod as well, managing to balance the sheer intensity of the instruments with the varied vocal performances, ensuring that nothing is lost in the cacophony. It’s a tightrope walk of dynamics, and the production team executes it with finesse.

In essence, “Kingslayer” is a defiant anthem of resistance, a collaborative effort that transcends language barriers and genre confines to deliver a message of empowerment. It’s a testament to the evolving landscape of metal, where traditional boundaries are being obliterated in favor of innovation and fusion.

So, light up, lean back, and let “Kingslayer” take you on a relentless ride through the future of metal. It’s a bold, brash statement piece from BMTH and BABYMETAL that not only showcases their individual strengths but also their collective power to break new ground. Vicious Shred? More like viciously shredding the rulebook and setting the stage for what’s next in the ever-evolving saga of metal music.

content.rendered:
Prepare to have your metal mindsets flipped, folks, because Nemophila’s “Odyssey” takes us on a voyage that’s as unexpectedly enchanting as it is a deviation from their usually thrash-heavy repertoire. This track isn’t just a song; it’s a saga. It’s like they’ve taken a detour through the realms of pop anthemics and cinematic soundscapes, emerging with a sound that’s both radio-friendly and robustly heartfelt.

“Odyssey” showcases Nemophila like we’ve rarely seen them before. Known for their bone-crushing riffs and maelstrom of metal fury, here they pivot, offering a composition that balances their inherent aggression with a surprising layer of melody and harmony that could easily resonate across the vast expanses of rock and pop domains. It’s a bold move, showing their versatility and refusal to be pigeonholed into a singular metal archetype.

The opening salvo of the song might fool the uninitiated into thinking this will be another relentless thrasher, but as the track progresses, it blossoms into an anthem that’s both uplifting and immense. The guitars, while still carrying the weight of Nemophila’s signature sound, are more melodious, weaving lines that soar rather than just shred. This isn’t to say they’ve abandoned their roots; the power and precision are still there, but they’re channeled into a form that’s more expansive and, dare I say, introspective.

The true surprise, however, comes with the chorus. It’s here that “Odyssey” really stakes its claim in the territory of anthems. The vocals elevate, transcending the boundaries of heavy metal to tap into a universal longing and determination that could easily place this song in the climactic scene of a blockbuster movie or blaring from the speakers of a festival main stage. It’s an anthem for the ages, bridging genres and inviting listeners from all walks of the music spectrum to join in the journey.

This pivot towards a more radio-friendly sound might raise eyebrows among purists, but it’s a testament to Nemophila’s artistic courage and their understanding that the spirit of metal is not confined to raw aggression alone. “Odyssey” embodies the band’s willingness to explore and evolve, integrating elements that showcase not just their technical prowess, but their ability to connect on an emotional level with a broader audience.

In “Odyssey,” Nemophila hasn’t just stepped away from their harsher, more thrashy tunes; they’ve leaped into a realm where their music can be both a battle cry and a beacon of hope. For better or worse, they’ve injected a dose of mainstream appeal into their sound, but they’ve done so without sacrificing the intensity and integrity that have defined them from the start.

So, whether you’re here for the shredding solos or the anthemic choruses, “Odyssey” is a reminder that in the world of music, the journey is just as important as the destination. Nemophila, with this track, invites us all to embark on an odyssey that’s not just heard but felt, resonating with a message of resilience and unity that transcends genre boundaries. Fire up your speakers, and let “Odyssey” take you on a voyage that defies expectations and redefines what a metal anthem can be in the modern era.

excerpt.rendered: “Odyssey” by Nemophila is a departure from their usual thrash-heavy style, delving into pop anthemics and cinematic soundscapes while maintaining their signature aggression. The track weaves melody and harmony with their powerful sound, crafting an anthem that transcends genre boundaries. It’s a bold move showcasing their versatility and emotional connection with a broader audience.

title.rendered: Some new Unleash the Archers, with the song “Ghost in the Mist”

As the song twists along with a solid bass line and elated melodic and harmony parts paired on guitar the video shows behind the scenes and related footage of the band. With the expected chuckles and smiles form the band. The video just adds fun to an already excellent song.

As things roll on, we get the treat to a tasteful solo wedged between – get this – BREAKDOWNS! Yeah, that’s right. Don’t ever expect Unleash the Archers to just churn out some song following average form.

title.rendered: Falling Back to 1996 with Nailbite and their song “Endless”

content.rendered:
Upon first encountering Nailbite’s “Endless,” I was immediately struck by the way it seems to encapsulate the zeitgeist of our era—an era marked by both relentless progress and profound existential questioning. It’s a track that, much like a well-designed piece of software, layers complexity under an interface of apparent simplicity.

“Endless” begins with a haunting guitar riff that sets the tone for the entire piece, reminiscent of the way a carefully thought-out user interface invites you into a new experience. The initial simplicity is deceptive, leading you into a labyrinth of emotional depth and technical proficiency. The guitar work, intricate yet accessible, reminded me of the elegance of a well-crafted code: complex in its logic but ultimately serving a clear and poignant purpose.

The vocals, raw and brimming with emotion, serve as the human element amidst the digital precision of the instrumentation. It’s akin to the narrative we often seek in technology—searching for humanity within the machine. The lead singer’s voice conveys a sense of longing and introspection, drawing the listener into a contemplative state, much like the process of debugging a challenging piece of code. There’s frustration, yes, but also the promise of resolution and understanding.

Lyrically, “Endless” navigates the themes of time’s cyclical nature and the human desire for meaning within that cycle. This is where the song truly resonates with the technologist’s soul. Just as we iterate over code, seeking improvement and understanding, the song iterates over emotions and questions, each chorus and verse building upon the last to deepen the inquiry.

The production of the song itself merits discussion. There’s a layered, almost architectural quality to it, with each instrument and vocal track carefully placed within the mix to build towards the climactic bridge. With the oddity of 90s era computer imagery and items heralded thoguhout. This acts as a moment of catharsis, much like the moment of an epiphany.

A fascinating song, video, and interesting band. Check em’ out!

The haunting guitar riff leads into emotional depth and technical skill, paralleling the elegance of well-crafted code. The vocals bring a human element, mirroring the search for humanity within technology. The song’s production and themes resonate with the iterative nature of life and technology, offering a reminder to appreciate the journey.

title.rendered: Another Reaction to Any Given Day & They Seem Pissed at “Come Whatever May”

content.rendered:
In the pantheon of metal music videos, there’s a spectrum that ranges from the solemnly serious to the unintentionally hilarious. Nestled comfortably in the middle, like a gunslinger at high noon, sits Any Given Day’s “Come Whatever May”. It’s a video that toes the line between earnestness and a tongue-in-cheek homage to the wild west, and it does so with the aplomb of a band fully aware of the tightrope they’re walking.

From the opening shot, we’re transported to a world that feels like Sergio Leone and Quentin Tarantino had a brainstorming session in a German metal band’s rehearsal space. The band members, clad not in traditional metal attire but in outfits that wouldn’t be amiss in a Spaghetti Western, set the stage for what’s to come. There’s a certain charm in watching a group known for their crushing riffs and guttural screams donning cowboy hats and bandoliers, striding through a landscape more commonly associated with tumbleweeds than mosh pits.

The song itself is a powerhouse of modern metal, with riffs that hit like a locomotive and a chorus that’s anthemic in its execution. Yet, it’s the video’s commitment to the wild west aesthetic that brings a layer of almost comical seriousness to the affair. There’s something inherently amusing about watching a metal band take on the roles of cowboys, engaging in shootouts not with bullets, but with the sheer force of their music. The video plays with these tropes knowingly, winking at the audience with every slow-motion strum and steely glare.

title.rendered: Join Me to React to Elli Berlin’s new song “Aus Der Asche” (From the ashes)

content.rendered:
Elli Berlin’s “Aus der Asche” translates to “From the Ashes” in English, a powerful title that evokes the imagery of rebirth, resilience, and transformation. This song, part of Berlin’s repertoire, showcases her unique ability to blend compelling melodies with evocative lyrics, creating a musical experience that’s both intimate and expansive.

The song’s lyrics are in German, but the music’s emotional depth and Berlin’s expressive delivery make it accessible to all listeners. The song’s arrangement is simple and elegant, with Berlin’s voice and guitar taking center stage. The song’s gentle, lilting melody is both soothing and haunting, creating a sense of intimacy and vulnerability that draws the listener in. The song speaks – in lyric and music – to the universal human experience of facing adversity, falling to our lowest points, and then finding the strength to rise again. “Aus der Asche” metaphorically uses the phoenix’s story, a mythological creature that is reborn from its ashes, to represent this cycle of destruction and renewal. It’s a powerful symbol of resilience, echoing the idea that from the end comes a new beginning.

Elli Berlin’s sensual sexuality is an integral part of her artistic expression, adding depth and nuance to the song’s narrative. Rather than being overt or explicit, it’s woven into the fabric of the music and the performance in a way that enhances the song’s themes of rebirth and transformation. It’s not just about the physical aspect of sexuality but about the power of creation, regeneration, and the intimate knowledge of oneself that comes from enduring and overcoming adversity.

The choice of “phoenix from the ashes” as a motif underscores the song’s message of hope and renewal. It’s a potent reminder that even in our darkest moments, there is the potential for growth and rebirth. The phoenix symbolizes not just survival, but the beauty and strength that can emerge from suffering. In “Aus der Asche,” Elli Berlin captures this duality of human experience—the pain of loss and the exquisite joy of finding oneself reborn, stronger, and more alive than before.

title.rendered: Reaction to The Gems “Send Me to The Wolves”

content.rendered:
When diving into “Send Me to The Wolves” by The Gems, you’re not just hitting play on a track; you’re strapping in for a straight-up, no-holds-barred rock and roll ride. This isn’t about reinventing the wheel; it’s about taking that wheel, greasing it up with some high-octane energy, and letting it rip down the highway of classic rock vibes with a modern twist.

Right from the get-go, the song grabs you with its gritty guitar riffs that are as raw as they are catchy. It’s like they’ve channeled the spirit of rock and roll’s golden years, wrapped it in a leather jacket, and unleashed it into the wild. The rhythm section doesn’t just back up the melody; it kicks down the door, making sure you’re tapping your foot, nodding your head, or, at the very least, feeling that irresistible urge to air-drum along.

The vocals are a beast all their own. There’s a rasp, a growl, and a howl that feels like it’s been dragged through the streets of rock’s storied past, picking up bits and pieces from the legends and making them its own. It’s a voice that doesn’t just sing; it tells a story, paints a picture, and drags you into the narrative, making you feel every high and low along the way.

Now, about the video – it’s good fun, plain and simple. It doesn’t try to overshadow the music with overly complex narratives or flashy effects. Instead, it complements the track’s energy in a way that’s just fun without being overwhelming or preachy. It’s the visual equivalent of a well-timed tasteful guitar solo: not the main focus but utterly satisfying and perfectly in tune with the song’s spirit.

In essence, “Send Me to The Wolves” by The Gems is a gem of the enduring allure of rock and roll. It’s a reminder that sometimes, all you need is a few chords, a compelling beat, and a voice that can weave it all together into something that feels both familiar and fresh. It’s a track—and a video—that doesn’t just aim to entertain but invites you to join in on the fun. And in the end, isn’t that what rock and roll’s all about?

“Burn Your Desire” by Ifa is a scintillating melody that catches you off guard, weaving its way into the fibers of your being. It’s an experience, a journey that Ifa embarks upon with the listener, inviting them into a world where desires aren’t just felt but set ablaze as the sometimes torturous landscape they are.

The exquisite production quality of “Burn Your Desire,” where every beat, every note, and every breath feels intentionally placed yet effortlessly natural. There’s a magic in the way the song builds up starting with a simmering ember of an intro that crescendos into a conflagration of sound and emotion. With the added spice of a video emblazoned, literally, with the fires of wraith lit upon shields of vengeance.

The composition is a masterful blend of delicate melodies and stirring harmonies that mirror the tumultuous journey from despair to liberation. Each chord and note seems meticulously chosen to resonate with the listener’s innermost feelings, creating a musical tapestry that is as intricate as it is beautiful. The arrangement flirts with the boundaries of genres, refusing to be pigeonholed, much like the indomitable spirit it seeks to portray.

Vocally, Ifa delivers a performance that is nothing short of transcendent. There’s a vulnerability in the delivery that’s palpable, a raw edge to the voice that speaks volumes of lived experience and authenticity. Yet, there is also strength, a defiant roar against the silence that often shrouds topics of abuse. This duality in Ifa’s vocal execution enriches the track, lending it a power that’s both haunting and inspirational.

Lyrically, “Burn Your Desire” is a poetic exploration of darkness and light. The song’s narrative navigates the shadows of suffering and the luminous path of rejecting and rising above it. There’s an elegance in how the lyrics confront such a difficult subject matter, never veering into the realm of despair, but instead, offering a message of hope and renewal. The use of metaphor and imagery in the songwriting elevates the track, transforming personal agony into a universal call to break free from the chains of the past.

title.rendered: A Hot Dog Reaction to Allegaeon’s new song “Iridescent”

content.rendered:
Allegaeon, a band known in the technical death metal scene, distinguishes itself not only through its impressive musicianship and intellectually driven lyrics but also by its unique approach to visual storytelling – or the hilarious lack thereof. Originating from Colorado, Allegaeon has forged a distinctive path by marrying complex musical compositions with narratives that delve into science, philosophy, and human history. Their sound—a compelling amalgamation of blistering solos, complex drumming, and a versatile vocal range—marries aggression with precision, setting them apart in a genre that demands both innovation and virtuosic skill.

Allegaeon’s musical oeuvre serves as a testament to their technical virtuosity, with each release further cementing their status as pioneers capable of pushing metal’s boundaries. Their tracks, characterized by instrumental virtuosity and thematic richness, invite listeners to engage with narratives that challenge both the intellect and the senses. This fusion of musical excellence and intellectual discourse has cultivated a dedicated fanbase, positioning Allegaeon as a beacon of both thought and thrash.

The release of “Iridescent” underscores Allegaeon’s commitment to blending technical mastery with profound conceptual themes married to the hilarious approach to Hot Dog videos and grand absurdity in their videos. This track is emblematic of all that, featuring a rich tapestry of guitar riffs that showcase a mastery over melody and aggression, coupled with Hot Dogs. The drum work complements this melodic interplay, propelling the song with a power that is both fierce and intricate. “Iridescent” is a testament to Allegaeon’s ability to navigate the delicate balance between intensity and harmony, presenting a piece that is both audibly and intellectually captivating that includes hot dogs!

Thematically, “Iridescent” traverses the realms of transformation and perception, utilizing the imagery of refracted light to explore the complexities of reality and identity, coupled with the complexity of choice between ketchup, mustard, and mayonaise. The song’s title and thematic exploration suggest a nuanced reflection on the myriad ways in which we understand and interact with the world and how sometimes, we slammed with a combination of ketchup and mustard, then lambasted with mayonnaise. This exploration is mirrored in the music’s dynamic shifts, which guide listeners through a spectrum of emotion and intensity.

However, what truly sets Allegaeon apart—particularly in the context of “Iridescent”—is their penchant for infusing their music videos with a blend of comedy, absurdity, and levity, even when tackling subjects of weighty significance. Not to mention the calm introduction of breasts, eating hot dogs, and the interplay of oddly placed innuendo inherent in such a hot dog of a situation. This approach reflects a profound understanding of the power of juxtaposition; the band adeptly uses humor to both engage and disarm their audience, making complex themes more accessible. The visual complement to “Iridescent” exemplifies this strategy, combining the song’s profound thematic undertones with visuals that are unexpectedly humorous and self-aware. This unique blend of heavy music with lighthearted visuals not only highlights Allegaeon’s versatility but also showcases their ability to connect with audiences on multiple levels.

Through “Iridescent,” Allegaeon continues to redefine the boundaries of technical death metal, marrying exceptional musicianship with a narrative depth that challenges and delights. Their ability to weave together humor with complexity ensures that their music remains both engaging and thought-provoking, reinforcing their status as innovators in the metal genre. For aficionados and newcomers alike, “Iridescent” serves as a luminous example of Allegaeon’s unique place within the metal pantheon—a band unafraid to explore the depths of human experience with both seriousness and a wink.

So when enjoying some hot dogs, be sure to tip your dog deliverer!

content.rendered:
Bruce Dickinson’s latest offering, “Rain on the Graves,” is a powerful testament to his enduring talent and unyielding passion for music. With its thunderous riffs and soaring vocals, the song serves as a reminder of why Dickinson is regarded as one of the most iconic figures in rock history.

From the moment the first chords ring out, “Rain on the Graves” grabs hold of the listener and doesn’t let go. Dickinson’s vocals are as commanding as ever, effortlessly weaving through the song’s dynamic shifts and emotive lyrics. The guitar work is equally impressive, delivering a relentless barrage of hooks and melodies that leave a lasting impression.

Thematically, “Rain on the Graves” explores the darker side of human nature, touching on themes of loss, redemption, and the passage of time. It’s a hauntingly beautiful meditation on the inevitability of death and the resilience of the human spirit, delivered with Dickinson’s trademark blend of introspection and defiance.

As the lead single for his upcoming project album, “Rain on the Graves” sets the stage for what promises to be a monumental release. The album, titled “Echoes of the Past,” sees Dickinson delving into a wide range of topics, from personal struggles to societal issues. Each song is a masterclass in songwriting, showcasing Dickinson’s ability to craft compelling narratives and unforgettable melodies.

Here’s a sneak peek at the track list for “The Mandrake Project”:

  5. Fingers in The Wounds

title.rendered: Poison Black Reaction, but Nixed Cuz Face Plant, Which One’s “Suffocated”

content.rendered:
Oh, Poison Black’s latest offering, “Fix Myself”, feels less like a song and more like a DIY project gone awry—where all the instructions were read backward and upside down. The track seems hellbent on burglarizing the cool of hip hop, the peppy essence of pop punk, and the visceral angst of Rage Against the Machine. Yet, despite these lofty thefts, all it manages to deliver is a staggering cargo of absurdity. Imagine a blender that instead of mixing, insists on separating its contents back to their original states—yes, it’s that fruitless and baffling.

“Fix Myself” attempts to stitch together a Frankenstein’s monster of genres, but alas, the creature refuses to come to life. Each musical segment, possibly kidnapped from better songs, struggles under the weight of its own identity crisis, never quite meshing into anything coherent. The end result feels like a musical ‘uncanny valley’—eerily familiar yet deeply off-putting. It’s as if the band set out with a map to the treasure chest of ‘ultimate cool’ but ended up digging in all the wrong places, hitting pipelines of cringe instead.

There’s a saying that ‘everything but the kitchen sink’ can work if done right; unfortunately, Poison Black not only threw in the sink but also the entire plumbing system, and none of it connected properly. So while the intent might have been to build a masterpiece, what we got was more akin to a hastily patched up draft that desperately needs revisiting. Or maybe, just maybe, it’s so avant-garde, it’s beyond mere mortal comprehension—but let’s not hedge our bets on that.

But Oh Wait, There’s MORE! Ok, I pulled the plug at that point… and switched to another song. So you get a 2 reactions for the price of one on this episode!

Which One – Suffocated

“Suffocated” by Which One encapsulates the all-too-familiar feeling of being trapped, not just in circumstance, but in one’s own spiraling thoughts. This track strikes a chord with its stripped-back sincerity, avoiding the common pitfalls of overproduction that can dilute the raw potency of emotional music. The vocals are a standout, delivering each line with a palpable urgency that doesn’t just aim for the ears but grips the heart with a firm, almost uncomfortable pressure.

The instrumentation is cleverly arranged—sparse yet effective, creating a haunting ambiance that lingers long after the song ends. Which One uses the simplicity of the music to their advantage, allowing the lyrics room to breathe and resonate. It’s a testament to the power of minimalism in music, where less truly becomes more.

“Suffocated” doesn’t need bells and whistles to convey its message; it’s all there in the unvarnished truth of the melody and words. This song is a sharp reminder of how overpowering and isolating the struggle with inner demons can be. Which One has crafted a piece that’s both a lament and a reflection, a musical introspection that feels deeply personal yet universally understandable.

title.rendered: It’s Brutal When Dreams Are Broken, but check out Enterprise Earth’s “Where Dreams Are Broken”!

The technical prowess displayed by the guitarists offers a slew of intricate riffs that weave through the punishing blast beats, showcasing not only speed but also precision and creativity. This complexity ensures that the track is not merely an onslaught but a carefully structured narrative of intensity.

Vocally, “Where Dreams Are Broken” features a performance that is both visceral and varied. The guttural lows and piercing highs communicate despair and ferocity, effectively conveying the song’s thematic darkness. The lyrical content, exploring themes of disillusionment and inner turmoil, adds a layer of emotional gravity to the track, engaging the listener not just sonically but also intellectually.

Moreover, the production quality of the song deserves commendation. Every element, from the oppressive breakdowns to the subtle atmospheric layers, is polished and balanced, allowing for a listening experience that is both overwhelming and clear.

In sum, “Where Dreams Are Broken” stands as a testament to Enterprise Earth’s ability to craft music that is as thought-provoking as it is heavy. It’s a track that doesn’t just demand attention—it commands it, making it a standout piece in the landscape of extreme metal.

title.rendered: I React to Discovering Vana and Her Song “Clandestine”

content.rendered:
After several listens to Vana’s “Clandestine,” each playthrough peels back another layer of its complex emotional fabric, revealing a song that resonates deeply with haunting introspection and dark poeticism. Initially, the song presents itself as an immersive exploration into themes of despair and the spectral vestiges of the self, which grow increasingly discernible and profound by the third listen.

Vana crafts “Clandestine” with a tapestry of somber lyrics, underpinned by a sound that is both atmospheric and foreboding. The opening verse, “I’m visionary / I’ve seen it in my dreams,” immediately sets the stage for a narrative that is intensely personal and introspective. The imagery of one’s own apparition reflecting back and the flickering lights in darkness evokes a profound sense of duality – the external perception versus the internal reality.

By the time the pre-chorus hits, the lyrical depth becomes overwhelming, “I can’t remember how it felt to be alive / And now I’m haunted by the thoughts of suicide.” These lines are a turning point where the narrative shifts from a vague dream-like state to a more distressing confrontation with one’s demons. The shift from viewing life in vibrant color to shades of gray metaphorically paints a picture of life losing its vibrancy, its essence slowly fading into the monochrome.

The chorus is where Vana’s lyricism shines brightest, utilizing the physical sensations of faintness and speechlessness to mirror the psychological and emotional turmoil within. “Now I’m feeling faint / Can’t think of words to say” suggests an overwhelming sense of existential weight that words fail to capture, while the imagery of wanting to “fade away” and “taste on my bullet” introduces a stark, chilling confrontation with mortality.

By the song’s final act, the refrain and repeated choruses serve not just as a lyrical recapitulation but as a deeper descent into the psyche. The refrain, “Bury me / Cover me in ashes,” conveys a desire to return to the earth, to escape the pain through a metaphorical death and rebirth. It’s a lyrical embodiment of the cycle of decay and growth, of dust returning to dust.

Musically, “Clandestine” complements its lyrical darkness with a moody, ambient sound that envelops the listener. The instrumentation is layered and not overly intricate, mirroring the complexity of the emotions being unpacked. However the focus is solely on her, bright amid the darkness of the snow, in a kind of modern sensualized candy for the viewer. The use of minor keys amid this video and her particular show is slow and deliberate pacing, which creates an almost claustrophobic atmosphere, enhancing the song’s themes of entrapment and escape.

Ultimately, “Clandestine” is a showcase in uncanny ways to the human condition’s darker sides, the hidden corners of our minds, and the shadows within that shape our existential experiences. It’s a song that doesn’t just aim to entertain but to evoke and provoke—a bold, artistic statement from Vana that lingers long after the last note fades.

title.rendered: I got curious and did some research. What are the top 10 subgenres in Heavy Metal?

content.rendered:
I got curious and decided to dig into subgenres in heavy metal. This is something that I don’t usually think too much on, since I don’t really stick the labels on bands too often, and when I describe them to other people I tend to describe just the band versus using the assumption of a genre it might fit into.

Without surprise, heavy metal being a diverse genre with numerous sub-genres, each offering a unique sound and style. Here are ten of the top sub-genres of Heavy Metal that I managed to collect:

Thrash Metal:

  • Fast tempo and aggression
  • Prominent bands: Metallica, Slayer, Megadeth, Anthrax

Death Metal:

  • Growled vocals, heavily distorted guitars, and blast beat drumming
  • Prominent bands: Death, Cannibal Corpse, Morbid Angel

Black Metal:

  • High-pitched shrieking vocals, tremolo picking, and dark themes
  • Prominent bands: Mayhem, Burzum, Darkthrone

Power Metal:

  • Melodic, fast-paced, and often features fantasy themes
  • Prominent bands: Helloween, Blind Guardian, DragonForce

Doom Metal:

  • Slow tempos, thick sound, and melancholic lyrics
  • Prominent bands: Black Sabbath, Candlemass, My Dying Bride

Progressive Metal:

  • Complex song structures, time signature changes, and virtuosity
  • Prominent bands: Dream Theater, Opeth, Symphony X

Symphonic Metal:

  • Combines heavy metal with symphonic elements like orchestras and choirs
  • Prominent bands: Nightwish, Epica, Within Temptation

Glam Metal:

  • Catchy hooks, anthemic choruses, and a focus on appearance and theatrics
  • Prominent bands: Mötley Crüe, Poison, Twisted Sister

Nu Metal:

  • Incorporates elements of other genres such as hip hop, grunge, and industrial
  • Prominent bands: Korn, Linkin Park, Slipknot

Folk Metal:

  • Combines heavy metal with traditional folk music instruments and themes
  • Prominent bands: Finntroll, Ensiferum, Eluveitie

Of all these, after reading probably a dozen articles on subgenres, I realized I was missing some of the key subgenres that I listen to these days.

Deathcore and metalcore are both distinct subgenres of heavy metal that combine elements from other genres to create their unique sounds. While they weren’t listed in the top 10 previously, they are significant subgenres within the metal community. Here’s where they fit:

11. Deathcore:

  • Description: A fusion of death metal and metalcore, characterized by heavy breakdowns, death growls, and blast beats.
  • Prominent Bands: Suicide Silence, Whitechapel, Carnifex

12. Metalcore:

  • Description: Combines elements of extreme metal and hardcore punk, featuring breakdowns, melodic riffs, and a mix of clean and screamed vocals.
  • Prominent Bands: Killswitch Engage, As I Lay Dying, Bullet for My Valentine

While deathcore draws heavily from death metal’s brutality and complexity, metalcore incorporates more melodic and hardcore punk elements, making each subgenre distinct yet closely related to the broader metal family. Specifically here are some of the top bands I’ve had on my playlists and their respective subgenres that I could sort out for each.

Enterprise Earth:

  • Subgenre: Deathcore
  • Description: Known for their heavy breakdowns, aggressive vocals, and technical instrumentation.

Inferi:

  • Subgenre: Technical Melodic Death Metal
  • Description: Combines complex, technical guitar work with melodic elements and death metal intensity.

Novelists:

  • Subgenre: Progressive Metalcore
  • Description: Incorporates progressive metal elements with metalcore’s breakdowns and clean/screamed vocals.

Erra:

  • Subgenre: Progressive Metalcore
  • Description: Blends progressive metal’s technicality and melody with metalcore’s heaviness and dynamics.

Architects:

  • Subgenre: Metalcore/Post-Hardcore
  • Description: Known for their melodic yet heavy sound, incorporating both metalcore and post-hardcore elements.

Monuments:

  • Subgenre: Progressive Metal/Djent
  • Description: Features complex rhythms, technical guitar work, and a blend of clean and harsh vocals, characteristic of djent.

Periphery:

  • Subgenre: Progressive Metal/Djent
  • Description: Pioneers of the djent movement, known for their polyrhythmic patterns, technical proficiency, and progressive songwriting.

Make Them Suffer:

  • Subgenre: Symphonic Deathcore
  • Description: Combines deathcore’s brutality with symphonic and orchestral elements, creating a unique soundscape.

Polaris:

  • Subgenre: Metalcore
  • Description: Known for their energetic metalcore sound, combining melodic and heavy elements with both clean and harsh vocals.

Born of Osiris:

  • Subgenre: Progressive Metalcore/Deathcore
  • Description: Blends technical and progressive elements with metalcore and deathcore influences, featuring synths and complex arrangements.

Up until I got back into collecting music again (i.e. back around this post) I’d not paid one iota to the subgenres and classifications of these bands. As far as I was concerned I listened to “heavy” music with a “progressive” tilt. Ohhh boy I was surprised then, for example, to find out that some of these bands are “Post-hardcore” (WTF?) or “progressive metalcore”. Those always just sounded nonsensical to me, but whatever, I guess they fit once you add in the nuanced characteristics of each of the genres.

Of all these my top 3 area easily

  1. Deathcore
  2. Technical Melodic Death Metal
  3. Metalcore

Oh yeah, I’ve become one of *those people* that are into the *core genres! 🤣

Whatever the case, that’s my little synopsis that I regularly rotate in my listening queue. Keep thrashing, and catch ya later. 🤘🏻

Some of the top subgenres include thrash metal, death metal, black metal, power metal, and more. Additionally, deathcore and metalcore are notable subgenres that combine elements from other genres. The post explores prominent bands and their respective subgenres, with the author expressing a newfound interest in these classifications.

title.rendered: Orbit Culture’s ‘While We Serve’: A Visceral Metal Masterpiece

content.rendered:
Orbit Culture’s “While We Serve” is an unrelenting sonic juggernaut that pulls no punches, both lyrically and musically. This track exemplifies the band’s mastery in blending heavy, groove-laden riffs with a visceral intensity that commands attention from the first note to the last. The prodding heaviness of the song is a testament to Orbit Culture’s ability to channel raw emotion into a finely tuned metal machine.

From the very beginning, “While We Serve” plunges the listener into a – DENSE – wall of sound, driven by crushing guitar riffs and thunderous drums. The opening riff is a churning behemoth, setting a dark, oppressive tone that underpins the entire track. This is not a song that offers respite – NO RESPITE – instead, it marches forward with an inexorable force, drawing the listener deeper into its labyrinthine structure.

The vocal delivery is a perfect match for the weight of the lyrics, alternating between guttural growls and anguished screams. The chorus is a particularly poignant moment, where the melodic lines soar above the tumultuous instrumentation, creating a stark contrast that enhances the emotional impact.

The recent video release from Orbit Culture’s Helsinki show captures the band at their most ferocious. The live performance amplifies the intensity of “While We Serve,” with the raw energy of the band translating seamlessly to the stage. The video’s production quality is top-notch, offering a dynamic view of the performance that highlights both the individual musicianship and the cohesive power of the band as a unit.

One of the standout elements of the live show is the band’s stage presence. The members of Orbit Culture are not merely playing their instruments; they are embodying the music. The synchronized headbanging, the visceral connection with the audience, and the unbridled passion in every note and scream create an immersive experience that is as electrifying to watch as it is to hear.

Orbit Culture’s “While We Serve” is a powerful statement, both in its recorded form and its live execution. The prodding heaviness of the song, combined with the band’s formidable stage presence, makes for an experience that is as thought-provoking as it is exhilarating. This track, and the accompanying live video, are a testament to Orbit Culture’s ability to push the boundaries of modern metal while staying true to the genre’s core principles.

title.rendered: Kittie ‘One Foot in the Grave’ Lyrics: Existential Dread and Defiance in Metal

content.rendered:
Kittie’s “One Foot in the Grave” is a visceral onslaught that bridges the raw aggression of metal with a dark, haunting atmosphere. The track is a prime example of the band’s ability to merge ferocity with melodic undertones, creating a soundscape that is both brutally intense and eerily captivating.

Right from the opening riff, “One Foot in the Grave” plunges the listener into a maelstrom of heavy, downtuned guitars and thunderous drums. The relentless pace is set immediately, with a chugging rhythm that drives the song forward with a sense of impending doom. This prodding heaviness is a hallmark of Kittie’s sound, and it is on full display here, pulling no punches as it grinds its way through the listener’s psyche.

The vocal delivery is a standout aspect of the track. Morgan Lander’s voice oscillates between guttural growls and soaring clean vocals, creating a dynamic contrast that enhances the song’s emotional depth. The chorus is particularly striking, with its haunting melody providing a stark counterpoint to the abrasive verses. This interplay between harsh and melodic elements is where Kittie truly shines, showcasing their ability to craft songs that are as multifaceted as they are powerful.

Lyrically, “One Foot in the Grave” delves into themes of existential dread and defiance. The words are delivered with a palpable sense of urgency, reflecting the band’s unwavering commitment to their message. The lyrics, combined with the relentless instrumentation, create an atmosphere that is both oppressive and liberating, capturing the listener in a whirlwind of sound and emotion.

The production of the track is top-notch, with each element finely balanced to maintain the song’s intensity without sacrificing clarity. The guitars are thick and crunchy, the bass is deep and resonant, and the drums are sharp and punchy, driving the song with unyielding force. The overall mix ensures that every nuance of the performance is heard, adding layers of complexity to the listening experience.

“One Foot in the Grave” is not just a song; it’s a statement. Kittie demonstrates their mastery of the genre, blending elements of death metal, groove metal, and melodic metal into a cohesive and compelling whole. The track is a testament to the band’s evolution and their ability to push the boundaries of their sound while staying true to their roots.

In live performances, “One Foot in the Grave” takes on an even more powerful dimension. The raw energy of the band, coupled with the intensity of the music, creates an electrifying atmosphere that is impossible to ignore. Kittie’s stage presence is commanding, and their ability to connect with the audience is a testament to their skill as performers.

“One Foot in the Grave” is a show of force that showcases Kittie at their best. It’s a track that demands to be listened to at full volume, with every note and scream resonating deep within. For fans of heavy music, this song is a must-listen, and for those new to Kittie, it’s the perfect introduction to a band that continues to redefine the boundaries of metal.

title.rendered: Reaction for the esoteric, shifting, compositionally migratory song Criminal by Rivers of Nihil.

content.rendered:
“Criminal” by Rivers of Nihil is an intricate piece that defies conventional song structures, demanding a deeper dive into its esoteric composition. This track evidence of the band’s ability to weave complex musical narratives while maintaining a cohesive and powerful auditory experience.

From the onset, “Criminal” immerses the listener in a soundscape that oscillates between the realms of progressive death metal and atmospheric rock. The introduction is a haunting blend of ambient textures and dissonant chords, creating an eerie atmosphere that sets the stage for the journey ahead. This initial calm is soon disrupted by a torrent of blast beats and intricate guitar riffs, showcasing the technical prowess of the band.

As the first verse unfolds, the vocals emerge with a raw, almost primal intensity. The interplay between the guttural growls and the melodic undertones provides a dynamic contrast that keeps the listener on edge. The verse transitions seamlessly into the chorus, where the melody takes on a more anthemic quality. Here, the band employs a soaring vocal line that is both powerful and emotive, cutting through the dense instrumentation like a beacon.

The genius of “Criminal” lies in its ability to shift gears effortlessly. Midway through the track, the breakdown arrives as a sudden, yet welcomed, change of pace. The rhythm section takes center stage, with the bass and drums locking into a tight, groove-laden pattern. This section is a masterclass in tension and release, as the minimalist approach amplifies the impact of the subsequent return to full-blown intensity.

The bridge section is where Rivers of Nihil truly flex their compositional muscles. A series of time signature changes and polyrhythms create a labyrinthine passage that demands close attention. The lead guitar work here is particularly noteworthy, with solos that are both technically impressive and emotionally resonant. These moments of virtuosity are balanced by sections of atmospheric calm, where the band allows the music to breathe and expand.

As the song approaches its climax, the elements introduced throughout the track converge in a cathartic finale. The final chorus is delivered with an added layer of urgency, the vocals reaching a fever pitch while the instruments drive relentlessly forward. The outro fades into a melancholic soundscape, a final nod to the band’s ability to blend brutality with beauty.

In “Criminal,” Rivers of Nihil have crafted a song that is as intellectually stimulating as it is viscerally satisfying. Each part of the composition, from the verses to the breakdowns, serves a purpose in the overarching narrative, creating a piece that is greater than the sum of its parts. This track is not just a testament to the band’s technical skill, but to their ability to convey profound emotion through complex musical structures.

content.rendered:
The recent collaboration between Lizzy Hale and Skid Row is nothing short of electrifying. When a powerhouse vocalist like Hale teams up with a band synonymous with the raw energy of ’80s rock, the result is bound to be explosive. The performance was a masterclass in rock synergy, with Hale’s commanding stage presence perfectly complementing Skid Row’s legendary sound. Her vocal prowess, characterized by its grit and range, brought a fresh dynamism to the band’s classic tunes. This collaboration didn’t just revive the nostalgia of Skid Row’s golden era but also injected it with a contemporary vigor that appeals to both long-time fans and new listeners.

“Youth Gone Wild”

Skid Row’s “Youth Gone Wild” remains an anthem of rebellion and youthful exuberance, even decades after its release. The song is a high-octane blast of energy that encapsulates the spirit of the late ’80s rock scene. With its infectious riff and Sebastian Bach’s raw, powerful vocals, “Youth Gone Wild” is a call to arms for the disenfranchised youth. The lyrics, which speak of breaking free from societal constraints and forging one’s path, resonate as much today as they did back then. This track is a perfect encapsulation of Skid Row’s identity—unapologetically bold, loud, and rebellious. Listening to it now, one can still feel the adrenaline rush, the call to defy norms, and the thrill of being young and wild.

“Riot Act”

“Riot Act” is another gem from Skid Row’s discography that showcases their ability to blend aggressive riffs with catchy hooks. The song’s relentless pace and gritty lyrics create an atmosphere of defiance and raw emotion. It’s a perfect example of how Skid Row could harness their hard rock roots while delivering a polished, radio-friendly sound. The track’s pounding drums and fiery guitar solos are complemented by Bach’s fierce vocal delivery, making “Riot Act” a standout in their repertoire. The song’s energy is infectious, and its rebellious spirit is palpable, making it a timeless piece that continues to inspire and energize listeners.

In both “Youth Gone Wild” and “Riot Act,” Skid Row demonstrates their knack for crafting anthems that are not only musically compelling but also thematically resonant. These songs capture the essence of a generation’s angst and desire for liberation, and their legacy endures as they continue to inspire new waves of rock enthusiasts.
